page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is an arm64-based general-purpose server instance powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 8 physical cores with 8 dedicated vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache resources consist of 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several multi-threaded and memory-bound workloads, contrasted with weaker single-core execution. The server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1812.89 and a multi-core score of 14472.4, both placing in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 563.91 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 87.42 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-threaded tasks show limitations, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1073.0 and Passmark CPU scoring 6205.54, both falling into the weaker performance tier. Cryptographic performance is also limited, as shown by a weak Passmark encryption score of 1300.22, despite hardware-level AES support.

The t2a-standard-8 is designed for scale-out workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. It demonstrates average efficiency in web serving, achieving a static web serving throughput of 10.09 GB/sec, and database operations, processing 10.91 million Redis SET operations per second. It is less suitable for machine learning tasks, as demonstrated by a poor text generation speed of 32.29 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM. Qualitatively, the ARM-based architecture provides a cost-efficient alternative to traditional x86 instances for multi-threaded workloads like software compilation and web serving, where high core density and steady-state performance are prioritized over peak single-core speed.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is an arm64 general-purpose instance featuring an 8-core Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz with 32 GB of RAM. Lacking hyperthreading, it provides 8 dedicated physical cores, each with 4.0 GB of memory. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks show average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14472.4 and a static web serving throughput of 10.09 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is weaker, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1073.0 and a poor LLM text generation speed of 32.29 tokens/sec. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for scale-out, multi-threaded workloads such as web serving, software compilation, and database operations, where dedicated physical cores offer predictable execution without the overhead of shared-core architectures.
